questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A particle moves along the x-axis with velocity v(t) = 4t - t² (SI units). It momentarily comes to rest at two instants. The magnitude of its displacement between these two instants is:
questions.explanation: Set v(t)=0 → t=0 and t=4 s. Integrate: x = ∫₀⁴(4t-t²)dt = [2t² - t³/3]₀⁴ = 32 - 64/3 = 32/3 m. Since v>0 on (0,4), distance equals displacement.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two blocks A (3 kg) and B (2 kg) are connected by a light inextensible string passing over a smooth fixed pulley. Block A rests on a smooth horizontal table and block B hangs vertically. The system is released from rest. Taking g = 10 m/s², the tension in the string is:
questions.explanation: For A: T = 3a. For B: 20 - T = 2a. Adding: 20 = 5a → a = 4 m/s². Thus T = 3×4 = 12 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A particle of mass 0.5 kg moves along the x-axis under a conservative force with potential energy U(x) = 2x³ - 6x² + 4x (SI units). If its speed at x = 0 is 4 m/s, its speed at x = 2 m is:
questions.explanation: Energy is conserved. At x=0: U=0, KE = 0.5×0.5×16 = 4 J. At x=2: U = 16-24+8 = 0. So KE remains 4 J → 0.25v² = 4 → v = 4 m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A uniform solid cylinder of mass M and radius R rolls without slipping down an inclined plane of height h. The ratio of its rotational kinetic energy to its total kinetic energy when it reaches the bottom is:
questions.explanation: For solid cylinder, I = 0.5MR². KE_rot = 0.5Iω² = 0.25Mv². KE_total = 0.5Mv² + 0.25Mv² = 0.75Mv². Ratio = 0.25/0.75 = 1/3.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: If the radius of Earth shrinks by 2% while its mass remains unchanged, the percentage change in the escape velocity from Earth's surface is approximately:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: One mole of an ideal monoatomic gas undergoes a cyclic process ABCA on a P-V diagram. AB is isothermal expansion from (P₀, V₀) to (P₀/2, 2V₀); BC is isochoric pressure increase back to P₀; and CA is isobaric compression back to V₀. The net work done by the gas in the cycle is:
questions.explanation: W_AB = P₀V₀ ln2 (isothermal). W_BC = 0 (isochoric). W_CA = P₀(V₀-2V₀) = -P₀V₀ (isobaric). Net = P₀V₀(ln2 - 1).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A conducting spherical shell of inner radius R and outer radius 2R carries a total charge +Q. A point charge +q is placed at its center. The electric potential at the outer surface of the shell is (k = 1/4πε₀):
questions.explanation: Induced charge on inner surface = -q; outer surface carries Q+q. Potential at r=2R from shell = k(Q+q)/2R. From point charge q at distance 2R = kq/2R. Total = k(Q+2q)/2R.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In a metre bridge experiment, the null point is obtained at 40 cm from the left end of the wire. If the resistance in the left gap is 8 Ω, the resistance in the right gap is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A proton moves with velocity v = (1.0î + 3.0k̂) × 10⁶ m/s in a uniform magnetic field B = 1.0k̂ T. Taking the mass of the proton as 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg and charge as 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, the radius of the helical path and the pitch are respectively:
questions.explanation: v_perp = v_x = 1.0×10⁶ m/s; v_parallel = v_z = 3.0×10⁶ m/s. r = mv_perp/(qB) ≈ 1.04 cm. T = 2πm/(qB) ≈ 6.56×10⁻⁸ s. Pitch = v_parallel×T ≈ 19.6 cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A 100-turn circular coil of radius 10 cm is rotated at 30 rpm about a vertical diameter in a uniform horizontal magnetic field of 0.1 T. The amplitude of the alternating emf induced in the coil is:
questions.explanation: ω = 30 rpm = π rad/s. A = π(0.1)² = 0.01π m². ε_max = NABω = 100 × 0.01π × 0.1 × π = 0.1π² = π²/10 V.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In a Young's double-slit experiment, the slit separation is d and the wavelength is λ. A thin transparent film of thickness t = 5λ and refractive index μ = 1.5 is placed in front of one slit. The central maximum shifts to the position originally occupied by the:
questions.explanation: Optical path difference = (μ-1)t = 2.5λ. Fringe shift = 2.5β. Position of 3rd dark fringe (n=2) is y = (2+0.5)β = 2.5β. Hence central max shifts to the 3rd dark fringe position.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The de Broglie wavelength of an electron accelerated through a potential difference V varies as:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A string of length 2.0 m consists of two parts: the first 1.2 m has linear mass density μ₁ = 1/16 kg/m and the remaining 0.8 m has μ₂ = 1/4 kg/m. The string is under a tension of 100 N. The lowest frequency at which standing waves can be set up in the composite string is:
questions.explanation: v₁ = √(100×16) = 40 m/s; v₂ = √(100×4) = 20 m/s. Frequency equality: n₁v₁/2.4 = n₂v₂/1.6 → n₁/n₂ = 3/4. Lowest integers n₁=3, n₂=4. f = 3×40/2.4 = 50 Hz.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Passage-based: In a second trial, glider A (0.4 kg) moves at 0.6 m/s and glider B (0.2 kg) is at rest. They stick together after collision. The percentage loss in kinetic energy is:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: For the reaction N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) → 2NH₃(g), ΔH = -92 kJ mol⁻¹. If the bond energies of N≡N and H-H are 946 kJ mol⁻¹ and 436 kJ mol⁻¹ respectively, the N-H bond energy is approximately:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following species has the largest ionic radius?
questions.explanation: All are isoelectronic (10 electrons). Ionic radius decreases with increasing nuclear charge: O²⁻ > F⁻ > Na⁺ > Mg²⁺.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: For the equilibrium PCl₅(g) ⇌ PCl₃(g) + Cl₂(g), Kp = 4.0 atm at 500 K. If the degree of dissociation is 0.5, the total pressure of the system is:
questions.explanation: At equilibrium: moles = 1.5 for α=0.5. Partial pressures: p_PCl₅ = p_PCl₃ = p_Cl₂ = P/3. Kp = (P/3)(P/3)/(P/3) = P/3 = 4 → P = 12 atm.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The major product formed when 2-methyl-2-butene is treated with HBr in the presence of peroxide is:
questions.explanation: Peroxide effect gives anti-Markovnikov addition. The Br radical adds to the less substituted carbon (C3) generating a more stable tertiary radical at C2. Final product: 3-bromo-2-methylbutane.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The IUPAC name of the complex [Co(NH₃)₅Cl]SO₄ is:
questions.explanation: Oxidation state of Co = +3 (from charge balance with sulfate). Anionic ligand is named chlorido. Correct name: Pentaamminechloridocobalt(III) sulfate.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is a non-reducing sugar?
questions.explanation: Sucrose (glucose α-1,2 fructose) has no free anomeric carbon and is non-reducing. Maltose, lactose, and cellobiose are reducing.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The standard electrode potentials at 298 K are: E°(Fe³⁺/Fe²⁺) = +0.77 V and E°(I₂/I⁻) = +0.54 V. The standard EMF and feasibility of the reaction 2Fe³⁺ + 2I⁻ → 2Fe²⁺ + I₂ are:
questions.explanation: E°cell = E°cathode - E°anode = 0.77 - 0.54 = +0.23 V. Positive E° implies ΔG° < 0; reaction is spontaneous.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The number of stereoisomers possible for 2,3-dichlorobutane is:
questions.explanation: Two stereocenters exist. Configurations: (R,R), (S,S), and meso (R,S) with a plane of symmetry. Total distinct stereoisomers = 3.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The shape of the XeF₅⁺ ion is:
questions.explanation: Xe in XeF₅⁺ has 6 electron pairs (5 bond pairs + 1 lone pair). VSEPR predicts square pyramidal geometry (AX₅E).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The correct order of reducing character of the oxyacids of phosphorus is:
questions.explanation: Reducing power depends on P-H bond count: H₃PO₂ (2 P-H) > H₃PO₃ (1 P-H) > H₃PO₄ (0 P-H).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The electrophilic substitution reaction of aniline with bromine water gives:
questions.explanation: The -NH₂ group is strongly activating and ortho/para-directing. With excess Br₂(aq), aniline undergoes rapid tribromination to give 2,4,6-tribromoaniline.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: For any hydrogen-like species, the ratio of the kinetic energy of the electron to its total energy in any stationary orbit is:
questions.explanation: From the virial theorem for Coulombic systems: KE = -TE and PE = 2TE. Thus KE/TE = -1 for any orbit.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A compound with molecular formula C₅H₁₀O gives a positive iodoform test and yields 2-methylbutane on Clemmensen reduction. The compound is:
questions.explanation: Positive iodoform test implies a methyl ketone. Clemmensen reduction of 3-methyl-2-butanone gives 2-methylbutane.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Passage-based: From the given initial-rate data for H₂O₂ decomposition catalyzed by I⁻, the rate law is:
questions.explanation: Comparing expts 1&2: [H₂O₂] doubles, rate doubles → 1st order in H₂O₂. Comparing expts 1&3: [I⁻] doubles, rate quadruples → 2nd order in I⁻. Rate law: k[H₂O₂][I⁻]².

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Passage-based: The rate constant k at 298 K is:
questions.explanation: Using rate = k[H₂O₂][I⁻]² with experiment 1: 1.2×10⁻⁶ = k(0.1)(0.1)² = k×10⁻³ → k = 1.2×10⁻³ M⁻²s⁻¹.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The distance between the parallel lines 3x + 4y + 5 = 0 and 6x + 8y + 15 = 0 is:
questions.explanation: Rewrite second line as 3x+4y+7.5=0. Distance = |5-7.5|/√(3²+4²) = 2.5/5 = 1/2.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: lim(x→0) (sin x - x)/x³ equals:
questions.explanation: Taylor series: sin x = x - x³/6 + O(x⁵). Thus (sin x - x)/x³ = -1/6 + O(x²) → -1/6.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: If α, β are the roots of x² + px + q = 0, the value of α²/β + β²/α is:
questions.explanation: α²/β + β²/α = (α³+β³)/αβ = [(α+β)³ - 3αβ(α+β)]/αβ = [(-p)³ - 3q(-p)]/q = (3pq - p³)/q.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: ∫₀^(π/2) sin²x cos³x dx equals:
questions.explanation: Substitute u = sin x, du = cos x dx. Integral becomes ∫₀¹ u²(1-u²)du = [u³/3 - u⁵/5]₀¹ = 1/3 - 1/5 = 2/15.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Three fair dice are thrown simultaneously. The probability that the sum of the numbers on their upper faces is at least 15 is:
questions.explanation: Total outcomes = 216. Favorable: sum 18(1 way) + 17(3 ways) + 16(6 ways) + 15(10 ways) = 20. P = 20/216 = 5/54.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The solution of the differential equation dy/dx = (x+y+1)/(x+y-1) is:
questions.explanation: Let v = x+y. Then dy/dx = dv/dx - 1. Equation becomes dv/dx = 2v/(v-1). Separate: (1 - 1/v)dv = 2dx. Integrate: v - ln|v| = 2x + C. Substitute back: x - y + ln|x+y| = C'.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The value of sin(π/14) sin(3π/14) sin(5π/14) is:
questions.explanation: Using co-function identities, the product equals cos(π/7)cos(2π/7)cos(3π/7). By the standard cosine product identity for n=3, this equals 1/8.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The normal to the parabola y² = 4x at a point P meets the parabola again at Q. If the ordinate of P is 2, the length of segment PQ is:
questions.explanation: P is (1,2) since y=2=2t → t=1. Normal at t: y + tx = 2t + t³ → y + x = 3. Intersection with y²=4x gives y² + 4y - 12 = 0 → y=2 (P) or y=-6 (Q). Q=(9,-6). PQ = √((9-1)²+(-6-2)²) = √128 = 8√2.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: ∫₀^π x sin⁶x cos⁶x dx equals:
questions.explanation: Using ∫₀^π x f(sin x,cos x)dx = π/2 ∫₀^π f dx for symmetric f, we get I = π ∫₀^(π/2) sin⁶x cos⁶x dx. Using sin⁶x cos⁶x = (1/64)sin⁶(2x) and Wallis formula, I = 5π²/2048.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The number of distinct arrangements of the letters of the word BANANA in which no two N's are adjacent is:
questions.explanation: Arrange B,A,A,A first: 4!/3! = 4 ways. This creates 5 gaps. Choose 2 gaps for N's: C(5,2)=10. Total = 4×10 = 40.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which organelle is the primary site of synthesis of proteins destined for secretion from the cell?
questions.explanation: The RER, studded with ribosomes, synthesizes proteins that are secreted or inserted into membranes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a dihybrid cross between AABB and aabb, the F₂ generation shows a phenotypic ratio of 9:3:3:1. This result demonstrates:
questions.explanation: The 9:3:3:1 ratio is the classic result of independent assortment of two unlinked genes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The photorespiration pathway in C₃ plants involves which three organelles?
questions.explanation: Photorespiration involves chloroplast (RuBP oxygenation), peroxisome (glycolate conversion), and mitochondria (glycine-to-serine conversion).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The plateau phase of the cardiac action potential is primarily due to:
options: Influx of Ca²⁺ balanced by efflux of K⁺
questions.explanation: Phase 2 plateau is caused by Ca²⁺ influx through L-type channels balanced by K⁺ efflux, maintaining depolarization.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a food chain, only about 10% of energy is transferred from one trophic level to the next. This is primarily because:
options: Most energy is lost as heat during respiration
Energy is created at each level
questions.explanation: The 10% law reflects that ~90% of energy is lost as metabolic heat through respiration at each trophic level.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The presence of homologous structures (e.g., forelimbs of whale, bat, and human) in different species is evidence of:
questions.explanation: Homologous structures indicate common ancestry and divergent evolution; analogous structures indicate convergent evolution.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In recombinant DNA technology, the enzyme used to join DNA fragments with complementary sticky ends is:
questions.explanation: DNA ligase forms phosphodiester bonds between adjacent 3'-OH and 5'-phosphate groups, joining DNA fragments.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A plant with genotype AaBbCc self-fertilizes. Assuming independent assortment, the probability that an offspring will be homozygous at exactly two of the three loci is:
questions.explanation: P(homozygous) = 1/2 per locus. Choose 2 loci: C(3,2)=3. Probability = 3 × (1/2)² × (1/2) = 3/8.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following diseases is an autoimmune disorder?
questions.explanation: Rheumatoid arthritis is an autoimmune disease where the immune system attacks joints. AIDS is immunodeficiency; malaria and typhoid are infectious.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The corpus luteum in the ovary primarily secretes:
questions.explanation: The corpus luteum secretes estrogen and progesterone to maintain the endometrial lining during the luteal phase.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: During which phase of the cell cycle does DNA replication occur?
questions.explanation: DNA synthesis (replication) occurs during the S phase of interphase.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Passage-based: In a predator-prey system, the time lag between prey and predator population peaks primarily indicates:
options: The predator's response time to changes in food availability
questions.explanation: The lag reflects the delay in predator numerical response (reproduction, recruitment) following changes in prey density.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Passage-based: If the rabbit population is artificially maintained at 90 per hectare by external feeding, the most likely long-term effect on the fox population is:
options: The fox population will stabilize at a new higher carrying capacity
The fox population will oscillate with decreasing amplitude
The fox population will initially rise, then crash due to overgrazing by rabbits
The fox population will remain unchanged
questions.explanation: Maintaining prey above carrying capacity causes habitat degradation (overgrazing), leading to eventual collapse of both prey and predator populations.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is a saturated fatty acid?
questions.explanation: Palmitic acid (C16:0) has no C=C double bonds and is saturated. The others are unsaturated.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: At a typical chemical synapse, if the extracellular Ca²⁺ concentration is reduced and Mg²⁺ concentration is simultaneously increased, the most likely effect on synaptic transmission is:
options: Increased neurotransmitter release due to enhanced vesicle fusion
Decreased neurotransmitter release due to competition with Ca²⁺ at voltage-gated channels
No change because Mg²⁺ can fully substitute for Ca²⁺ in exocytosis
Increased postsynaptic depolarization independent of presynaptic Ca²⁺
questions.explanation: Ca²⁺ is essential for vesicle fusion. Mg²⁺ competitively blocks Ca²⁺ channels but cannot trigger exocytosis, so neurotransmitter release decreases.
